title: SceneDocument
description:
A persistent scene source. IDs are authored ASCII names, never runtime IDs.

Loading sets no count budget; bulk pixels and geometry
belong in files beside the scene. Prefabs share scene-wide
assets across their placements.
Unknown fields are rejected to expose authoring mistakes. Arrays retain
authored order when serialized, yielding stable, readable source diffs.

animations.description: Keyframed clips that entity `animation` players play.

environment.description:
The scene's atmosphere and rendering effects. With it the scene
owns the whole look: instantiation sets every section, omitted ones
to the engine defaults. Without it the game's own settings stay.

prefabs.description: Reusable local entity trees. Definitions share this document's assets.

skins.description: Joint lists that deform skinned meshes.

streamed.description:
Entities that exist only near the camera: each root
with its descendants is one item, which world streaming spawns when
its cell comes within range and despawns when it leaves. Parents,
animation targets and skin joints stay within an item; IDs differ
from `entities`'. No terrains.

textures.description: Opaque sRGB pixels: inline base64, or image files.

AtmospherePreset.description: A starting point for an atmosphere; fields set beside it override it.

AuthoredPlacement.description: An object an author stands on the surface.

align.description: How far it leans with the ground: 0 upright, 1 along its normal.

asset.description: Its asset, by ID of the surface's assets.

level.description:
The pyramid level whose tiles hold it: 0, the finest; coarser for
objects seen from farther away.

position.description:
Its base's terrain-local point `[x, z]`, where it stands on the
ground.

sink.description: How deep its base sinks, in meters at scale 1.

yaw.description: Its turn about the vertical, degrees.

Biome.description:
A biome: where it applies (`fitness`, everywhere when omitted), the
layers of its ground and how wet its ground is (`wetness`, dry when
omitted). Later biomes paint over earlier ones where they fit; the first
covers wherever none of the others do.

wetness.description:
How wet its ground is, from 0, dry, to 1, soaked: darker and glossier
as water fills its pores and films it, the more so the rougher it
is. The ground takes the wetness of each biome as far as that biome
applies; the steep layer painted over them leaves it as they make it.

BiomeLayer.description:
One layer of a biome's ground. A biome's first layer covers its whole
ground.

mask.description: Where it paints over the layers before it.

material.description: The material painted, an ID of the surface's materials.

Blend.description:
How a layer's heights combine with the heights of the layers before it,
weighted by the layer's coverage: added, the higher or lower of the two,
or replacing them.

oneOf.description: Under gravity, contacts, water and wind: physics writes its pose.

Along the poses written to it, pushing dynamic bodies aside as it
goes: platforms, doors, paddles.

Cover.description: The cover growing where a surface material lies.

color.description:
The linear color of the blades' tips; roots take the ground's.
Lusher ground darkens and greens them, drier ground pales them.

density.description:
Blades per square meter where the material lies alone, on ground
halfway between dry and lush: lusher ground grows more, drier
ground fewer.

height.description:
The shortest and tallest blades, meters, shortest first, on
ground halfway between dry and lush: lusher ground grows them
taller, drier ground shorter.

sway.description: How far they lean in the wind: 0 stiff, 1 the most.

width.description:
Blade width at the root, meters: blades grow at their density
while this spans a pixel or more on screen. As they shrink under
a pixel each one left stands as a tuft as wide at its roots in
all as the blades it replaces, in leaves as wide as their roots,
or up to a tenth as wide as they are tall, as grass leaves are.

DebugViewMode.description: What a debug view shows each pixel as.

oneOf.description: The shaded image: no debug view.

What drew it, a color per kind: meshes gray-blue, placed objects
teal, impostor cards magenta, virtual geometry violet, terrain brown,
ground cover green, water blue, the sky pale blue.

Its level of detail, from the finest: red, orange, yellow, green,
cyan, blue, violet and gray, for meshes and placed objects (their own
mesh, then each simplification) and terrain's patches alike;
impostor cards magenta, virtual geometry a color per cluster. Frames
GPU presentation draws (`capture` with `alpha` and `gpu`) show levels
and cards as play does; exact frames draw every mesh whole.

Impostor cards magenta (cards fading over their meshes pink) over
everything else gray: where cards stand in for meshes.

Which sun shadow lookup decided it: the clipmap's levels green to
blue, from the finest, a terrain's horizon purple, where no level is
drawn gray; darker where it lies in shadow, black without sun
shadows.

How it casts sun shadows: meshes red, placed objects orange,
virtual geometry violet, impostor cards casting cards of their own
magenta, terrain brown, what casts none gray.

How many fragments passed the depth test there as the frame drew,
from dark blue (one) through green and yellow to white (ten or more).

Its shading normal, as colors: x red, y green, z blue, each from 0
(pointing back) to 1 (along the axis); terrain's its smooth
surface's.

Terrain's level-0 tiles and patches (sixteen samples a side): tile
edges red, patch edges dark, the ground between gray; everything else
as in `cards`.

Terrain's surface materials, each in its own color, blended in the
shares the ground shows them in.

The share of the sky terrain's ground sees, unlit, from black (none)
to white (all of it).

How terrain's ground shows its materials' maps: green where their
detail shows, filtered over the pixel, yellow as that filtering
averages their normal maps' slopes into roughness, red where a whole
repeat spans less than a pixel and their means stand in, blue where it
shows as its cover's canopy.

How deep terrains' water stands, tiles' and simulated alike, from
pale (none) through blue (half a meter) to navy (two meters or
more), on a square-root scale. The water's views draw water wherever
it lies, however little of the pixel it covers, and show the sea,
falls' sheets and everything else gray, the sky dark, all unlit.

How fast the water runs, from dark violet (still) through crimson to
yellow (six meters a second or more).

Its Froude number, its speed over its shallow waves' (√(g·depth)):
calm water from deep blue (0) to pale cyan, shooting water from
yellow to red (3 or more), water running at its waves' speed (1)
black.
How turbulent it runs, from dark teal (0) through green to lime (1).
Where white water is born, from dark blue (none) to white (1).

The reach of the stream it runs in, by the stream's slope: pools
blue, plane beds cyan, steps and pools green, cascades orange, falls
red; water no stream holds (lakes) violet.

The foam it carries, as its flow churns it up, carries it and loses
it (`engine_terrain::shallow_water`), from dark brown (none) through
sand to white (the most water carries).

How far across its water body is, the fetch the wind has over it: a
river's width, a lake's equal-area diameter, on a logarithmic scale
from violet (a quarter meter) through teal (32 meters) to pale
yellow (4096 meters or more).

Its eddies' turbulent Froude number: the speed they turn at,
(g·U·S·depth)^(1/3) for its speed U and its surface's slope S, over
√(g·depth); from dark (calm) through orange, where they start
breaking its surface white (`engine_terrain::BREAK_ONSET`), to white,
where they break it white all over (`engine_terrain::BREAK_FULL`).

The roughness its shading gives its surface, from black (0, a
mirror) through copper to white (1): calm water's, widened by the
slopes of the waves a pixel hides.

The wind's speed over it, gusting and sheltered by the terrain
upwind, as a share of the free wind's: from dark (still air) through
azure (the free wind) to white (twice the free wind, a gust's most).

Deformer.description:
Presses tracks into deformable ground as a scene's `deformer`
field: each fixed tick, while its entity's world position lies at most
`contact` meters above the terrain under it (or below it), it presses a
footprint from where it pressed the tick before. Put it where an object
meets the ground: a wheel's or a foot's lowest point.

contact.description: Meters above the terrain within which it presses.

depth.description:
Meters it sinks ground as deformable as that along its middle,
deeper by however far it lies below the ground.

flatness.description:
Its footprint's shape: 0 round, deepest along its middle like a
wheel's rut; 1 flat, a foot's or a plate's level floor.

radius.description: Meters across the footprint it presses.

ErosionLayer.description: A layer that erodes the layers below it.

creep.description:
Square meters of hillslope creep each round, at most about a
quarter of the square of the level's spacing: the most an
explicit step keeps stable.

debris.description:
How fast the debris flows of steep headwaters scour each round,
on top of the rivers: their erodibility times the time step for
each unit of slope, so they cut as the square of the slope where
stream power cuts as the slope, and steep slopes carve gullies
rather than stand smooth.

incision.description:
How fast rivers cut each round: the stream power law's erodibility
times its time step.

level.description:
The pyramid level whose samples it erodes: finer levels wear finer
valleys and take longer.

Facing.description:
How far the ground tilts toward a compass heading: the slope's
tangent times the cosine of the angle between the ground's downhill
direction and the heading, 0 on level ground, positive on slopes
facing the heading and negative on slopes facing away. A ramp of
`[-0.3, 0.3]` covers slopes of about 17 degrees facing away through to
slopes of about 17 degrees facing toward it.

heading.description:
The heading, in degrees from -z toward +x, as views give yaw: 180
faces +z, south where north lies at -z.

ramp.description: The tilts toward the heading its ramp runs between.

FarPlacement.description:
Where a placement layer also stands far away: on the tiles of a
coarser level, every one of its objects, where its own level's tiles
are not resident.

level.description: The coarser level whose tiles hold them.

GivenRiver.description:
One river given: the line it runs along, from upstream, and what its
data says of its channel. Its width, depth and discharge each hold
one value for the whole river or one for each of its points; what it
leaves out the bake derives, as for its own courses.

depth.description:
Meters its channel's middle lies below its banks; omitted, as
deep as downstream hydraulic geometry stands a channel its flood
fills.

discharge.description:
Cubic meters a second its bankfull flood carries, which fills its
channel to its banks; omitted, what the area draining into it
brings, as its hydrology layer's discharge says.

name.description: Its name, as its data or its author calls it.

points.description:
Terrain-local meters along x and z it runs through, from
upstream: it runs along the smooth line through them.

width.description:
Meters across its channel from bank to bank; omitted, as wide as
downstream hydraulic geometry stands a channel its flood fills.

Grounded.description:
Stands its entity on the terrain: its translation's y is
kept `offset` meters above the ground under its x and z. Unparented
entities only; without a resident tile under it (or over a hole) the
entity keeps its translation, as walking navigation agents keep theirs:
their walks stand them, on bridges' decks too.

offset.description: Meters above the ground its translation stands.

HummocksLayer.description:
Earth hummocks (thúfur): frost heaves wet, fine soil under turf into
mounds with troughs between them, on gentle ground. They are the
blobs of gradient noise whose lattice spans a hummock and a trough;
levels whose samples lie further apart than a hummock is across, the
shortest wavelength they resolve being two samples, hold the ground
they stand on.

cover.description:
The share of the ground its ramps allow that its patches cover:
0 none, 1 all.

height.description: Meters from the troughs to the tallest hummocks' tops.

patches.description: Meters across the patches it lies in.

seed.description: Picks the pattern of its patches and hummocks.

slope.description:
Slopes (degrees) over which it fades in, none at the first and
all from the second: falling, so it keeps to gentle ground, where
frost heaves the soil up rather than drawing it downhill into
lobes.

wetness.description:
Wetness indexes over which it fades in, none at the first and all
from the second: where water gathers in the soil frost heaves.

HydrologyLayer.description:
A layer that bakes where water runs over the layers below it and cuts
channels into them: the rivers the rivers layers below it give, then
those it finds where the water left gathers.

discharge.description:
Cubic meters a second each square kilometer drained brings the
channels full to their banks: every channel whose flood is not
given carries this times the area draining through it, which sets
how wide and deep its channel stands where that is not given, as
channels full to their banks widen and deepen downstream.

level.description:
The pyramid level whose samples the bake reads: rivers are traced
along its grid, and begin where their channels span two of its
samples from bank to bank, the narrowest water settling over
samples that far apart holds; its maps and lakes lie over the
landscape [`MAP_LEVELS`] levels coarser. Finer levels trace narrower
channels more closely and take longer.

Interior.description:
An interior's light, blending in over the probe's blend distance inside
its faces.

sky.description: The share of the sky's light that reaches surfaces inside the box.

sun.description: The share of the sun's light that reaches surfaces inside the box.

MacroCauses.description:
How strongly each cause tints a surface's macro colors
([`crate::macro_colors`]): the share of its brightness the ground
gains or loses where the cause is whole, in the cause's own hue; 0
turns the cause off. Plants grow lusher as far as the causes darken
the ground and drier as far as they pale it. The causes the bakes and
the ground's shape find move it by 15 percent and more, past the
light's spread within a patch, so they read from afar; the noise's
patches stay faint, as strong noise reads as camouflage.

aspect.description:
Slopes turned to the sun's side ([`Self::heading`]) dry out paler
and warmer, and those turned from it stay damp, darker and
mossier, as far as the direct sun they take differs from level
ground's.

broad.description:
The noise's broad patches, a few hundred meters across, lighter
and darker.

deposit.description:
Ground erosion laid down holds deep soil, built up over the bakes'
whole span: darker and browner with humus, its plants lusher, as
floodplains and the feet of slopes are. Lakes' shores show paler,
sandier grains the waves keep washed.

dust.description: Dust settles paler and warmer within six meters of roads.

heading.description:
The sun's side, toward the midday sun: degrees from -z toward +x,
as views give yaw. 180, +z, keeps north at -z, as views assume:
the midday sun stands south of the northern mid-latitudes; 0
turns it north for the southern ones.

patchy.description:
The noise's finer patches, some 45 meters across, lighter and
darker.

relief.description:
Ridges, wind-scoured and thin-soiled, weather paler and lichened;
hollows hold shade and deep soil, darker and browner.

steep.description:
Slopes from 30 degrees to 50 hold thin soil over rock, which
shows through it paler and grayer.

warmth.description:
The noise's widest patches, some 600 meters across, warmer and
cooler: the share red gains or loses, blue moving the other way.

wet.description:
Wet ground, where water gathers and runs as the hydrology bake
found it and along lakes' shores, darkens as water fills its pores
(Lagarde 2013): porous ground soaked keeps a fifth of its albedo,
the damp ground of hollows and banks about seven tenths.

worn.description:
Ground erosion wore away shows the paler, grayer subsoil and rock
under the humus-dark topsoil it lost.

Mask.description:
A value from 0 to 1 at every sample, from the sample's height, slope,
the way it faces, curvature and position, and what the terrain's bakes
and roads hold there: where a biome applies, where a material covers
its biome's ground, or how wet a biome's ground is. Ramps run from 0 at
their first value to 1 at their second, smoothly, falling when the first
is the larger.

oneOf.description: The same value everywhere.
A ramp over meters above the terrain's origin.

A ramp over the ground's slope, in degrees from level: the smooth
surface's through its samples ([`SampleShape`]).

A ramp over the ground's curvature: how fast its slope grows per
meter, positive in hollows and valleys, negative on ridges (the
smooth surface's Laplacian, [`SampleShape`]).

A ramp over how far the ground tilts toward a compass heading, on
the smooth surface through its samples ([`Facing`]).

A ramp over the meters the terrain's erosions wore the ground down
there, summed over its erosion stages, smooth between their samples:
positive, 0 where they laid ground down or left it, and without
erosion. `[0, 4]` rises over the first four meters valleys and
gullies cut.

A ramp over the meters the terrain's erosions laid down there,
summed over its erosion stages, smooth between their samples:
positive, 0 where they wore ground away or left it, and without
erosion. `[0, 2]` rises over the first two meters of sediment on
valley floors and fans.

A ramp over the base-10 logarithm of the area draining through the
ground, in square meters, as the terrain's hydrology bake found it:
channels begin near its channel area. 0 without one.

A ramp over the bake's wetness index, ln(a / tan b): about 5 on
steep ground, 10 and more in hollows and along streams.
A ramp over how deep water would stand in a filled pit, in meters.

A ramp over meters from the nearest river's edge,
negative in its water: `[2, 0]` covers river beds with two meters of
banks. Beyond every river's reach (sixteen meters past its edge),
and without rivers, it reads 1e9.

A ramp over the median size of the grains (the d50) of the bed of
the river holding the ground, in meters: `[0.002, 0.064]` rises from
sand through gravel to cobbles. Outside every river's bed (which
reaches a meter past its banks), and without rivers, it reads 0, as
fine as any grain: a ramp falling toward fine grains covers that
ground too unless a `river` or `flood` mask keeps it to the beds.

A ramp over the stream power of the river holding the ground at its
bankfull flood, in watts per square meter of its bed: `[150, 400]`
covers the beds of torrents strong enough to roll boulders. Outside
every river's bed (which reaches a meter past its banks), and without
rivers, it reads 0.

A ramp over meters the ground stands above the bankfull flood level
of the river holding it, negative below it: `[0.5, 0]` covers the
ground that river's floods reach, fading out over half a meter above
them. Outside every river's bed (which reaches a meter past its
banks), and without rivers, it reads 1e9.

A ramp over meters from the nearest road's edge,
negative on roads: `[1, 0]` covers roads with a meter of soft edge.
It averages the ramp across each sample's footprint, so roads
narrower than coarse levels' samples fade there instead of breaking
into dashes. Further than 32 meters beyond every road's shoulders,
and without roads, it reads 1e9.
Gradient noise from 0 to 1.
The product of masks.
The sum of masks.
The smallest of masks.
The largest of masks.
One minus a mask.
A mask remapped by a ramp: 0 up to `from`, 1 from `to`.

MeshSource.description: Supported geometry recipes, including arbitrary validated triangle meshes.

oneOf.description: Centered unit square in the XZ plane, facing +Y.
An engine mesh buffer file (`EMB1`) beside the scene.

A virtual mesh file (`EVG1`) beside the scene: a
cluster hierarchy renderers draw as the clusters each view needs, and
elsewhere as its most detailed cut of at most `fallback_triangles`
triangles (4096 when omitted). Built by `cargo xtask asset import`
for dense meshes.

NavAgent.description:
Walks its entity over the terrain under it to `destination`. Changing
the destination searches anew; none stands still.

destination.description: Where it walks to: world x and z.

level.description: The pyramid level it searches over: 0 the finest.

max_slope.description: The steepest steps it climbs: rise per meter.

max_water.description: Meters of water it wades through at most.

offset.description: Meters its origin stands above the ground.

turn.description: Degrees a second it turns at most.

NoiseLayer.description:
Procedural ground: fractal gradient noise whose fine octaves fade on
slopes (Quilez's derivative damping), optionally folded into ridges and
warped sideways, shaped toward wide valley floors, then cut by the
erosion filter's gullies running down its slopes.

blend.description: How the layer combines with the layers below it.

erosion.description: How deep gullies cut down slopes: 0 none.

height.description: Meters from the lowest to the highest ground before gullies.

offset.description: Meters added to every height of the layer.

ridges.description: 0 rolls; 1 folds every octave into sharp ridges.

roughness.description:
How much each finer octave keeps of the coarser one's height, from
0 (smooth slopes up close) through 0.5 (every scale alike) to 1
(rugged).

seed.description: Picks the pattern: the same seed gives the same heights everywhere.

smoothing.description: How much fine detail fades on slopes.

valleys.description:
0 keeps the heights' spread; 1 widens valley floors and sharpens
peaks.

warp.description: How far the ground warps sideways, as a share of the wavelength.

NoiseMask.description:
Gradient noise from 0 to 1, summed over octaves each half as long and
half as strong.

PathLayer.description: A road or track along the ground.

bridge_fill.description:
Meters the road would fill above the ground beyond which it bridges
instead, as it does over rivers and lakes; 0 never bridges.

points.description: Terrain-local meters along x and z the road runs through.

shoulder.description:
Meters on each side over which the road eases back into the
ground.

smoothing.description:
Meters along the road over which its height averages the ground's:
longer is gentler, cutting deeper and filling higher.

tunnel_cut.description:
Meters the road would cut into the ground beyond which it tunnels
instead; 0 never tunnels.

PlacementChoice.description:
An asset a placement layer chooses, by ID of the surface's assets, and
how often against the layer's others.

weight.description: How often it is chosen against the layer's others.

PlacementLayer.description: One layer of objects on a surface.

align.description:
How far its objects lean with the ground: 0 upright, 1 along its
normal.

bed.description:
How far around them they rest on, in meters at scale 1: 0, the
ground at their point; objects on steep slopes then stand in it
instead of hanging over it.

density.description:
Objects per hectare where everything allows, at most one per
footprint square.

downhill.description:
How strongly its objects turn their length, their meshes' x
axis, down the ground's slope: each points the way of its random
turn, a unit vector, plus the ground's downhill gradient (the
slope's tangent, pointing downhill) times this. Level ground
leaves them at random and steeper ground turns them further
downhill, as fallen trees lie: where the gradient times this
reaches 2, every one within thirty degrees of downhill. 0 turns
them at random everywhere.

far.description: Where it also stands far away.

level.description: The pyramid level whose tiles hold its candidates: 0, the finest.

materials.description:
The surface materials it stands on (IDs; any when empty),
weighted by their share.

scale.description: Its objects' scale range, the smaller first.

sink.description:
How deep they sink, in meters at scale 1, below the lowest ground
within their bed.

Remap.description: A mask remapped: 0 up to `from`, 1 from `to`, smooth between.

RiversLayer.description:
Rivers given over the terrain: lines its developer draws, or an
import tool writes from vector data, which the hydrology bake after
it runs as its courses, sized as they say, deriving only what they
leave out and the courses of water no given river gathers. `source`
and `attribution` (up to 1024 characters each) record where they
came from and the credit their data requires, as the import tool
writes them.

precision.description:
Meters its rivers' lines may stand off their true middles, as
precise as their data is: the bake moves each point that far at
most across its line toward the lowest ground, never over a rise;
0 keeps them where they are given.

SceneAmbientOcclusion.description: Ambient occlusion; an intensity of 0 turns it off.

intensity.description:
How much creases and corners darken the ambient light; 0 turns it
off.

radius.description:
World distance within which geometry occludes, the same at every
distance: where it shrinks on screen to what the finest occupancy
map's texels span where that map hands over, the occlusion fades
out, as the maps and terrains' probes hold coarser shade.

SceneAnimation.description:
A named animation clip: keyframed channels of the entities `targets`
names. Its channels are inline or in an `EAN1` buffer file (`uri`).

targets.description:
Entity IDs a channel's `target` index names. A player inside a prefab
placement resolves them against the placement's local IDs first.

SceneAtmosphere.description:
Sun, sky, fog and grade: a preset and the fields that
differ from it. Colors are linear RGB and may exceed 1.

aerial_color.description: The color distant ridges fade into away from the sun.

aerial_density.description: Aerial extinction per world unit at height zero; 0 turns it off.

aerial_falloff.description: How fast the air thins with height, per world unit.

aerial_glow.description:
How strongly distant ridges fade into a glow of the sun's color
toward the sun.

aerial_start.description:
Aerial perspective begins this far from the camera (world
units): beyond it, air dims what lies behind it toward the light
it scatters. Unlike fog it is unbounded and spans kilometers.

ambient.description: Scale of the sky's ambient light on surfaces.

contrast.description:
Contrast around mid grey after tone mapping: the slope of an
S-curve that keeps black and white; 0 flattens, 1 keeps it, and
the curve is steepest at 1.5.

emission.description:
Scale of material emission: how strongly lamps, lit windows and
other artificial lights show in this light, dim by day and full
at night.

fog_density.description: Fog density per world unit at height zero.

fog_falloff.description: How fast fog thins with height, per world unit.

fog_start.description: Fog begins this far from the camera (world units).

ground.description:
Sky color below the horizon: downward surfaces take their
ambient light from it.

horizon.description:
Sky color at the horizon: vertical surfaces take their ambient
light from it.

preset.description: The preset the other fields override.

rim.description:
Silhouette light in the horizon color, facing away from the
camera.

saturation.description: Saturation after tone mapping; 1 keeps it.

shadow_tint.description:
Hue of dark tones after tone mapping (split toning), as a color
gain scaled to keep luminance; white, like black, keeps them.
Cool shadows against warm highlights read as vivid.

specular.description:
Scale of sun highlights and sky reflections; 1 is physically
based.

sun_direction.description:
Direction toward the sun; any nonzero length, normalized when
rendered.

vibrance.description:
Saturation added to muted colors more than to vivid ones; 0 adds
none.

zenith.description:
Sky color straight up: upward surfaces take their ambient light
from it.

SceneAutoExposure.description:
Auto exposure: the eye adapting to the light in view. Each frame a
meter reads the frame drawn (a grid of samples, the middle of the view
counting more than its corners and the sky less than the rest) and
averages their light in stops, leaving out shares of the darkest and
the brightest. Later frames' exposure, eased quickly when the view
grows brighter and slowly when it grows darker, as eyes do, rises over
the atmosphere's authored exposure by two parts. The time of day's:
under the physically based sky, its own adaptation to its light (up to
4 stops), but at most `night` stops with the sun 14 degrees or more
below the horizon, easing there from 4 degrees below, so dusk dims as
before and night keeps dark. The view's: that average against what the
light falling on level ground gives an open view, beyond a stop either
way, so a cave by day brightens and a view of the bright sky darkens;
at night dark views stay dark. Opt-in.

brighten.description:
The most stops a dark view raises exposure, as a cave by day; none
at night, easing as the time of day's limit does.

center.description: How many times what the view's corners count the middle counts.

compensation.description:
Stops added to the exposure: positive brightens the view,
negative darkens it.

darken.description: The most stops a bright view lowers exposure.

night.description: The most stops the time of day raises exposure at night.

skip_bright.description: The share of the brightest samples it leaves out (the sun, lamps).

skip_dark.description: The share of the darkest samples the meter's average leaves out.

sky.description: How much the sky counts against what stands under it.

strength.description:
How far exposure follows the view: 0 not at all, 1 brings its
average all the way to within a stop of what its light gives an
open view.

to_brighter.description:
Seconds over which exposure goes most of the way (all but 1/e)
toward its new value after the view grows brighter.

to_darker.description: The same after the view grows darker.

SceneBloom.description: Bloom; an intensity of 0 turns it off.

intensity.description: How strongly light glows beyond bright pixels; 0 turns it off.

threshold.description: Exposed brightness above which light glows.

SceneCamera.description: Right-handed, Y-up perspective camera. Lens values are in world units.

far.description: The far plane's distance, at least 0.001 beyond the near plane's.

fov_degrees.description: Vertical field of view in degrees.

target.description: What it looks at, at least 0.001 from its position.

SceneChannel.description: One keyframed property of one target.

times.description: Key times in seconds, strictly increasing.

values.description:
Values, three numbers each (four for rotations, as quaternions x, y,
z, w); cubic splines give in-tangent, value and out-tangent per key.

SceneClouds.description: The cloud layer. Opt-in: a scene without a `clouds` section has none.

base.description: The world height of its base, meters.

coverage.description: How much of the sky it covers: 0 clear, 1 overcast.

in_view.description:
Whether the view marches the clouds after the opaque scene: then
they stand in front of whatever lies beyond them, all around a camera
inside the layer and below one above it, and the dome shows them
behind every surface only while the camera is under the layer.

resolution.description:
The dome's texels around the horizon; a quarter as many from the
horizon up.

scale.description: The meters across its largest shapes.

shadows.description: How much of the sun's light its shadows take from the ground.

slices.description: The frames over which ordinary frames march the whole dome.

wind.description: The wind it drifts in, meters per second along x and z.

SceneCollider.description:
A collider or sensor on any authored node, including prefab instance roots.
Zero layer masks are valid and intentionally disable matching pairs.

SceneColliderShape.description:
Explicit local collision geometry. Parent transforms apply as full affine
matrices; rendering meshes never supply implicit collider dimensions.

half_extents.description: Positive half sizes on local axes.

radius.description: Local radius. Nonuniform transforms form ellipsoids.

SceneDebugView.description:
Debug view settings: what frames show each pixel as, for agents and
people finding out why a pixel looks as it does. Off by default; a
view draws with its own pipelines, created the first time it shows,
and leaves screen effects, decals, transparent surfaces and temporal
antialiasing out.

shade.description:
Whether its colors darken where surfaces turn from the sun, so
shapes read.

SceneDecal.description:
A decal on this entity.

Its box is the entity's local unit cube (`[-0.5, 0.5]` on each axis):
scale the entity to size it. The material's color, base color map,
roughness, metalness and emission span the box's x and z, projected
down its y onto the opaque surfaces inside it that face its +y.

blend.description: How the decal combines with the surface it lies on.

fade_degrees.description:
Degrees between a surface's normal and the box's +y beyond which
the decal fades out, gone at 90.

material.description: ID of the projected material in this document.

SceneDecalBlend.description: How a decal combines with the surface it lies on.

oneOf.description: Covering by alpha, lit like any surface: paint, posters, markings.

Multiplying the surface's color, keeping its light: dirt, cracks,
stains and scorch marks.

max_decals.description:
An optional budget of decals a frame draws; beyond it the decals
nearest the camera win. Omitted, every decal draws.

extent.description: The meters of ground the map around the camera spans.

max_stamps.description:
An optional budget of stamps the log keeps, the oldest dropping
beyond it.

persist.description:
Whether the log keeps the stamps the map moves away from, so tracks
are there when the camera returns.

refill.description:
The seconds tracks take to refill to about a third of their depth;
0 never.

resolution.description:
The map's texels along a side; renderers keep fewer where the
device's buffers cannot hold them.

rim.description: How high the ground rises beside a track for its depth.

SceneDither.description:
Dithering: every write of color into an 8-bit target (the canvas, the
screen effects' scene and temporal antialiasing's history) adds noise
of about one step of what the target stores, so smooth gradients such
as dusk skies, fog and dark interiors show no bands, and temporal
antialiasing's history settles on the color instead of stopping a few
steps short. The noise is fixed per pixel, and turns every frame under
temporal antialiasing, which averages it. Off by default.

SceneDynamicResolution.description:
Dynamic resolution settings: whether display frames scale the size
they draw at, between the least and the most scale, so their GPU
time keeps within a budget. It goes by two timestamps a frame where
the device times its work, else by the time between frames; it lowers
the scale at once while frames run over the budget and raises it a
step at a time while they run under, in steps that keep temporal
antialiasing's history steady. Off unless a scene names it; hosts
turn it on for play in a window or a page, and keep it off for
offscreen captures and measured runs.

budget_ms.description:
Milliseconds of GPU time each frame keeps within; omitted, the
display's refresh interval where the host knows it, else a
sixtieth of a second.

enabled.description:
Whether display frames scale the size they draw at to keep within
the budget.

max_scale.description: The most scale frames draw at on each axis.

min_scale.description:
The least scale frames draw at on each axis, of the size the
resolution policy and the user's scale give: at most `max_scale`.

SceneEmitter.description:
A particle emitter on this entity.
Omitted fields take the engine's defaults.

acceleration.description: World acceleration: gravity, buoyancy or wind.

blend.description: How particles combine with what is behind them.

color.description: Linear RGBA at birth and at death; alpha fades.

direction.description: Direction of emission in the entity's local space; nonzero.

emission.description: Brightness multiple of the color, for glowing particles.

offset.description: Birth position in the entity's local space.

radius.description: Radius of the ball particles start in.

seed.description: Varies random choices between otherwise identical emitters.

size.description: Diameter at birth and at death, in world units.

speed.description: Initial speed in world units per second.

spread_degrees.description:
Half-angle of the cone of initial directions, in degrees; 180 emits
in every direction.

stretch.description: Seconds of travel particles stretch along their motion.

SceneEnvironment.description:
A scene's look. In a document, every omitted section takes the
engine's default state (opt-in sections: off); in a development
control, omitted sections stay as they are. Each section is the
engine's settings type, which documents its fields.

SceneFloating.description:
Rides the sea: each fixed tick the entity rises and falls with the sea's
surface under it and leans about its own heading. Unparented entities
only; nothing moves without an enabled sea.

draft.description: Meters of it below the surface.

tilt.description: How far it leans: 0 upright, 1 with the surface's normal.

crown_depth.description:
Meters into a crown over which the sun's light halves: masked
leaves and needles, and the cards baked from them, take the sun
through their crown from its sun-facing side, down along the
sun and across from where the crown meets sunlit air, instead
of the first caster toward the sun shadowing them whole; 0
turns it off.

ground_blend.description:
Meters up from the ground over which plants' color and light
blend into the ground's at their base; 0 turns it off.

hashed_cutoff.description:
Whether masked leaves dissolve over their texture's coverage on
temporally antialiased frames, a threshold turning across pixels
and frames instead of the material's cutoff.

transmission.description:
Sunlight leaves, needles and blades pass toward the eye, seen
against the sun through them, tinted by their color and shaded
as the sun is; 0 turns it off.

variation.description:
How far each plant's leaves stray from its material's color, by
a hash of where it stands, along a gradient from drier to deeper
green; bark keeps its color. 0 turns it off.

density.description: Scales every cover's density. Blades sway in the world's `Wind`.

max_blades.description:
An optional budget of blades and tufts a frame; beyond it the
farthest drop.

SceneGrounding.description:
How the base of an object standing on terrain blends into the ground:
how many units of its mesh up from where it enters the ground its
surface takes the ground's color, roughness and slope, from the
ground's slope under it.

SceneHaze.description:
Haze: distant surfaces fade into the sky behind them, and the near
air glows where the sun lights it. Fog and the air take the sky's own
light, blurred, in each view's direction (looking down, the sky's just
above the horizon, so far ground melts into the lit haze there), and
the air begins at the eye, at least as thick as `visibility` asks,
thinning with height as the atmosphere's (or the physically based
sky's) air does, as thick as `strength` makes it. Within `reach` of
the eye each view marches the fog and the air for the sunlight they
scatter toward the eye, concentrated around the sun by `forward`,
where shadows and the clouds' shadows let the sun through; there the
air's density drifts with the wind in patches about `size` across,
`spread` either side of its mean. Beyond the reach the glow of the
sun the sky's light holds stands in for it. Shadows are optional:
without them the sun lights all of the near air.

enabled.description:
Whether fog and the air take the sky's light, and the near air
the sun's.

forward.description:
How strongly the near air scatters the sun's light forward, the
asymmetry of its phase (Henyey and Greenstein's, as Mie
scattering's): 0 scatters it alike every way, higher concentrates
it around the sun.

reach.description:
The distance (world units) along each view over which the near
air's sunlight is marched, shadowed; 0 leaves all of it to the
sky's glow.

size.description:
The size (world units) of the near air's largest patches; patches
half and a quarter as large drift within them.

spread.description:
How far the near air's density strays from its mean in its
drifting patches, as a share of it: 0 not at all, 1 from clear to
twice as thick.

strength.description:
How thick the air is, as a multiple of what `visibility` (or the
atmosphere's own air) makes it: 0 clear, 1 as thick as that.

visibility.description:
The distance (world units) at which the air leaves a fiftieth of
what lies level with the eye; 0 takes twice the view's far
distance, so the world fades into the sky before it ends. The air
is never thinner than the atmosphere's own.

SceneHeightmap.description:
An imported heightmap: a file of little-endian 16-bit samples, row by row
along z (`.r16`), `width` by `height` of them, spanning `size` meters
from terrain-local `min` (x and z). Samples 0 to 65535 map to heights
`low` to `high`; the layer fades in over `falloff` meters inside its
edges and combines by `blend`. `source` and `attribution` (up to 1024
characters each) record where its heights came from and the credit
their data requires, as the `terrain_import` tool writes them.

cap.description:
The exposed brightness local lights' highlights ease toward
while `capped`, in the units of the bloom's threshold: unchanged
up to half of it, approaching it above; 0 caps none.

capped.description:
Whether local lights' highlights ease toward `cap`, sized or
not; the sun's stay as they are.

enabled.description:
Whether highlights take their lights' sizes: the sun's disk and
local lights' spheres and tubes.

light_radius.description:
The radius of the sphere local lights shine from where theirs is
smaller ([`crate::LocalLight::radius`]), world units: no lamp is a
point.

sun_size.description:
The sun's angular radius, degrees, while the physically based sky
is off; with it on, the sky's own `sun_size`.

SceneLevelOfDetail.description:
Level of detail settings: whether instances draw
simplified levels of their meshes, and impostors, where the
simplification stays within a pixel error.

fade_seconds.description:
Seconds placed objects take to fade between how the camera shows
them, from 0 (at once).

impostor_pixels.description:
The size below which placed objects draw their impostor cards:
the pixels of the viewport height their bounding spheres span.
Their frames hold as many texels across, rounded up to a power
of two, so cards are not magnified where they take over, and
their atlas's memory grows with its square. Larger shows cards
nearer; cards fade in over `fade_seconds`.

impostors.description: Whether draw groups draw impostors where they fit.

max_impostors.description: The most impostors kept resident; omitted for no budget.

pixel_error.description:
The largest simplification error a drawn level may show, in pixels
of the viewport height: smaller draws finer levels farther away.

SceneLight.description:
A point or spot light on this entity.
On an entity with a mesh it follows the mesh's displayed pose.

length.description:
The length of the tube it shines from, up the entity's local y axis
from its position, scaled with it; 0 for none. Spots shine from
their sphere alone. Lights take it while the environment's
`highlights` are on.

offset.description: Position in the entity's local space, scaled with it.

radius.description:
The radius of the sphere it shines from while the environment's
`highlights` are on, scaled with the entity (by its local y axis's
scale); their `light_radius` where this is smaller.

range.description: World distance beyond which the light has no effect.

region.description:
Where it shines: everywhere, or only inside or only outside
interiors (interior reflection probes' boxes).

spot.description: A cone; omitted for light in every direction.

SceneLightRegion.description:
Where a light shines: interiors are the boxes of interior reflection
probes.

oneOf.description: Inside and outside interiors alike.
Inside interiors only: a cave's or a hall's lamps.
Outside interiors only: lamps beside a cave's mouth.

distance.description:
View distance beyond which local light fades out: distant lights
cost no shading.

intensity.description: Scales every light's intensity, e.g. to dim lamps by day.

lights_per_cluster.description:
An optional budget of lights one view cluster lists. Omitted, every
light reaching a cluster shades there.

max_lights.description:
An optional budget of lights a frame shades; beyond it the nearest to
the camera win. Omitted, every light shades.

SceneMap.description:
A material's use of a texture: its ID, or a map with glTF sampler and
`KHR_texture_transform` settings.

SceneMaterial.description:
One named material; color channels are linear values in `[0, 1]` and
alpha is 1. `opacity` below 1 draws it transparent unless `alpha_mode`
says otherwise. glTF's texture maps, emissive color, alpha modes and
double-sided surfaces complete it; `surface`
roughness and metalness are glTF's roughness and metallic factors.

alpha_cutoff.description: With `mask` only: alpha below it is not drawn; default 0.5.

alpha_mode.description:
How alpha (opacity times base color texture alpha) is
used. Default `blend` below opacity 1, `opaque` otherwise.

double_sided.description: Draw back faces too, lit from their own side.

emissive.description:
Emitted linear color, not negative (glTF's emissive factor
times its emissive strength).

foliage.description:
Shade as foliage whatever the alpha mode: green reads as leaf,
needle or blade, which the sun lights through and each plant tints.
Masked materials shade as foliage either way; default false.

grounding.description: How the base of objects terrains place blends into the ground.

ior.description:
With `transmission`: the index of refraction in `[1, 3]`;
default 1.5.

metallic_roughness_texture.description: Linear green multiplies roughness and blue metalness.

normal_scale.description: Scales the normal map's deflection; default 1.

normal_texture.description: A tangent-space normal map (green up the image).

occlusion_strength.description: How much the occlusion map darkens, in `[0, 1]`; default 1.

opacity.description:
The fraction of light behind it the surface covers, in `(0, 1]`.
Below 1 it draws transparent, blending in any order,
writing no depth and casting no shadow. With
`alpha_mode` `mask` it is the alpha the cutoff tests.

surface.description:
How the surface responds to light beyond its color; without it the
material is matte.

texture.description:
Base color texture: its sRGB color multiplies `color`. A texture ID,
which repeats, or a map with sampler and transform settings.

thickness.description:
With `transmission`: the depth in world units of the
volume beneath the surface that bends rays; default 0, a thin wall.

top.description:
A layer settling on faces turned up, such as moss,
lichen, dust or snow.

transmission.description:
The share of light passing through the surface instead of
diffusing off it, in `[0, 1]`, tinted by its color (
glTF `KHR_materials_transmission`). Transmissive materials draw in
the transparent pass; the environment's `refraction` bends what shows
through them.

windows.description:
Divides the material into rooms, this many across its
base color texture's width and square in its texels: while the
environment's `windows` are on, each room's light comes on at its own
time around dusk. In `[1, 4096]`.

world_tiling.description:
Lays the maps from the world's axes, one repeat every
this many meters, instead of by texture coordinates:
no seams and one texel density at any size, for surfaces that stay
where they are, such as rocks. In `(0, 10000]`.

SceneMesh.description: A named CPU mesh. Sources contain no filesystem paths or executable data.

samples_per_tick.description:
The samples of search work each fixed tick does at most over every
walk being searched.

SceneNightSky.description:
The night sky and the sky's high veil: stars turning with the time
of day, where the sky behind them is dark; the moon, which the time
of day places (without one there is none) and the sun lights, giving
its phase, and whose light brightens the physically based sky's
night; and thin cirrus high above at any hour. Opt-in.

cirrus.description: How much of the sky cirrus covers: 0 none.

cirrus_drift.description:
How far cirrus' strands drift each second along x and z, world
units.

cirrus_height.description: How high above the eye cirrus floats, world units.

moon.description: How bright the moon is: 0 hides it, 1 is the full moon's.

moon_age.description:
The moon's age as a share of its month: 0 new, 0.5 full, waning
toward 1.

moon_size.description:
How large the moon shows, as a multiple of its usual size (twice
the true moon's, as the eye reads it).

star_density.description: How many stars show, as a multiple of a clear night's.

stars.description: How bright the stars are: 0 hides them, 1 is a clear night's.

SceneObject.description:
One local transform, optional renderable, or prefab instance root.
Tags are game-defined startup hook names.

animation.description: Plays an animation on its targets.

collider.description: Local collision shape, independent of rendering.

decal.description:
Projects a material onto the opaque surfaces inside this entity's
box.

grounded.description:
Stands on the terrain: its translation's y becomes
`offset` meters above the ground under it. Roots only.

name.description: Optional display label, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes without control characters.

nav_agent.description: Walks over the terrain to a destination. Roots only.

parent.description: Parent ID in the scene, or in this prefab's local definition.

prefab.description: Named prefab to expand below this transform-only instance root.

prefetch.description:
Names it a place the camera may be sent to, whose
terrain workers generate ahead of need.

reflection_probe.description:
Captures this entity's surroundings into an environment map that
surfaces inside its world box reflect.

rigid_body.description:
Moves as a rigid body: by gravity, contacts with the world's
solids and other bodies, and the water and wind about it, its
shape its collider's. Roots only.

skin.description:
The skin deforming this object's mesh. Requires a mesh with
joints and weights.

spline.description: One of this document's meshes bent along a curve.

tags.description: At most 16 distinct authored IDs, each at most 64 ASCII bytes.

terrain.description: A heightfield terrain whose tiles stream around the camera.

tint.description:
Multiplies this object's color and opacity channel by channel,
each factor finite and in `[0, 1]`.

SceneOcclusionCulling.description:
Occlusion culling settings: whether GPU-presented frames draw what the
last frame showed, test every other frustum-visible instance against a
depth pyramid of those depths, then draw only what it does not hide.
Output is unchanged; hidden instances cost no drawing. On by default.

enabled.description: Whether GPU-presented frames cull occluded instances.

levels.description:
Maps around the detail eye, the finest first, each read where a
pixel's size picks it: covers darken out to `radius` times two to
one less than their count, fading out over the outer half of the
coarsest map's reach.

radius.description:
Meters around the detail eye the finest map holds: each coarser
one reaches twice as far.

resolution.description:
Each map's texels a side, a multiple of 32: the cells its window
follows the eye by, sixteen a side, span whole texels, and each
cell of a finer map whole texels of the next.

strength.description: How much of the sky light full cover takes away.

choppiness.description: How sharply crests stand: 0 round swells, 1 nearly breaking.

clarity.description: The meters of water through which half the light passes.

color.description: The color deep water scatters back, linear.

level.description: The height of the still sea, world meters.

reach.description: The meters from the camera the sea draws.

seed.description: The seed of their headings and phases.

wind.description:
The wind that raised it, meters per second along x and z: its speed,
from 0.5 to 30, sets the waves' height and length and its direction
heads them.

SceneParticleBlend.description: How particles combine with what is behind them.

oneOf.description: Covering by alpha, lit by the sun and sky: smoke, dust, rain.
Adding light, unlit: sparks, fire.

Balls of mist, soft through their depth, lit by the sky and the
sun they scatter forward: spray, steam, fog banks.

max_particles.description:
An optional budget of particles a frame draws; beyond it the emitters
nearest the camera win. Omitted, every emitter draws.

air_density.description:
Kilograms a cubic meter of air weighs: what the wind drags
bodies with.

enabled.description: Whether bodies move; off, each holds where it stands.

gravity.description:
Every body's acceleration, meters per second squared: by default
the pull the terrains' water runs and falls by.

iterations.description:
Constraint solver iterations a tick: more keep stacks and piles
stiffer, at their cost.

water_density.description:
Kilograms a cubic meter of water weighs: bodies in water are
buoyed by the weight of what they displace and dragged with its
current, so those lighter than it float.

ScenePlayer.description: Plays a clip on its targets from this entity.

speed.description: Playback rate: 1 is real time, 0 paused, negative backward.

ScenePrefab.description:
A reusable entity tree whose parents reference IDs within the definition.

Instance roots use [`SceneObject::prefab`]. Template roots become children of
that instance root. Nested prefab references are deliberately unsupported.

SceneReflectionProbe.description:
A reflection probe on this entity.

Its box is axis-aligned in world space and centered on the entity's
world position, so the entity's rotation and scale leave it unchanged.
Surfaces inside it reflect what the probe captured from its center
(still objects and still lights), fading out over `blend` toward its
faces into the probes around it or the sky.

blend.description:
World distance inside the box's faces over which the probe fades
out.

extent.description: Half the box's size along each world axis in world units.

interior.description:
Makes the box an interior: a cave or a hall letting in
only these shares of the sky's light and the sun's.

faces_per_frame.description:
Cube faces captured per frame while probes wait: more fill new places
sooner, fewer keep those frames lighter.

max_probes.description:
An optional budget of probes kept captured; beyond it the probes
nearest the camera win. Omitted, as many as the GPU's texture arrays
hold.

resolution.description:
Texels across each face of every environment map, the sky's
included.

SceneReflections.description:
Screen-space reflections; an intensity
of 0 turns them off.

intensity.description: How strongly glossy surfaces reflect the screen; 0 turns them off.

max_roughness.description:
Surfaces rougher than this across the view, the way their
mirrored lobe stays narrowest, reflect only the sky: their
reflections of the screen fade out over its last fifth.

SceneRefraction.description:
Refraction through glass; a strength
of 0 turns it off.

blur.description: Blur radius in pixels that fully rough glass reaches.

strength.description:
Scales how far rays bend through transmissive materials; 0 turns
it off.

SceneResolution.description:
The user's resolution scale: display frames draw at this share of
the size the resolution policy gives the view on each axis, within
the display's own size, and upscale to the display. 1 by default.

scale.description:
The share of the resolution policy's size display frames draw at
on each axis: below 1 draws fewer pixels, above 1 more where the
display holds them.

SceneRigidBody.description:
A rigid body: physics moves its entity by gravity, its contacts with
the world's solids (terrain, placed objects, bridge decks and
colliders) and other bodies, and the water and wind about it. Its shape
is its entity's collider, scaled by its transform; its mass is that
shape's volume times its density, so bodies lighter than water float.
Roots only. Each fixed tick physics writes a dynamic body's pose to its
transform, which interpolates between ticks; a pose written to it
since moves it there. Bodies where the ground under them is not
resident hold still until it is.

density.description:
Kilograms a cubic meter: water's is 1000, wood's about 600,
stone's about 2600.

drag.description:
Its drag coefficient: how hard water's current and the wind push
on the area it turns to them.

fast.description:
Swept between ticks, so it stops at thin solids however fast it
moves.

friction.description: How its surface grips what it slides on.

restitution.description: How much of its speed into a contact it bounces back with.

spin.description: Its spin as it joins, radians a second about the world's axes.

velocity.description: Its velocity as it joins, world meters a second.

SceneShadows.description: Sun shadows; omitted fields take the engine defaults.

atlas_slots.description:
Tiles the atlas holds; tiles pixels read beyond these show a
coarser level.

finest_texel.description:
World size of the finest level's texels: shadows are this sharp
at most, where pixels are smaller.

levels.description:
Levels of the clipmap around the camera, each with texels twice
the size of the one inside it: sixteen reach from the finest
texel to about a kilometer a texel.

moving_tiles.description:
Tiles moving casters draw over each frame at most, coarse levels
first; they cast nothing on the tiles past these.

redraw_budget.description:
Tiles a frame redraws at most, coarse levels first; the rest
redraw over the next frames, a coarser level showing meanwhile.

tile_texels.description:
Texels along a side of a tile, the square that takes memory and
redraws.

SceneSkin.description:
A named skin: the joint entities that deform skinned meshes
and each joint's inverse bind matrix (column-major, sixteen numbers).

inverse_binds.description: One matrix per joint; identity when omitted.

joints.description: Joint entity IDs, resolved like animation targets.

SceneSky.description: A physically based sky. Defaults are Earth's. Opt-in.

adaptation.description:
How far exposure adapts to the sky's light, so that dawn, dusk and
night stay readable: 0 not at all, 1 fully.

aerial.description:
How far air hazes what lies away from the camera, as a multiple of
real distance; 0 none.

altitude.description:
The height of the world's origin above the ground of the planet,
meters.

mie_g.description: The forward lobe of Mie scattering's phase.

mie_height.description: The height over which Mie scattering thins by e, kilometers.

ozone.description: Ozone absorption per kilometer at its densest, 25 km up.

rayleigh.description: Rayleigh scattering per kilometer at the ground: red, green, blue.

rayleigh_height.description: The height over which Rayleigh scattering thins by e, kilometers.

sun_intensity.description: The sun's intensity: its color's scale above the air.

SceneSkyOcclusion.description:
Sky occlusion settings: the sky's light, and its reflections, fade
where still meshes hide the sky, so caves, tunnels and buildings go
dark inside away from their openings. Only meshes of entities that
stay still hide the sky, while shadows are enabled: not terrain, not
what terrain placement layers place, not moving or skinned meshes,
virtual geometry, particles or water. A cave must be a mesh of its
own.

directions.description:
Directions of the sky looked along: 5, 9 or 13, others round down
to one of them. Fewer cost less; more give smoother light near
openings.

enabled.description: Whether the sky's light fades where still meshes hide the sky.

far_distance.description:
Meters from the camera within which meshes hide the sky at all,
through coarser maps beyond `near_distance` (texels a 192nd of
it), fading out over a third as far again: farther, sky light is
as without sky occlusion.

floor.description:
The share of the sky's light a point keeps however little sky
it sees: 0 lets the deepest cave go black; a little more stands
in for light bouncing in from lit surfaces.

near_distance.description:
Meters from the camera within which sharp maps decide whether
meshes hide the sky, their texels a 192nd of it (0.25 m at 48 m):
shorter is sharper, for small rooms and narrow openings, longer
keeps more of the view sharp.

strength.description:
How much of the sky's light, and of its reflections, hidden sky
takes away: 1 all of it, 0 none.

SceneSpline.description:
A mesh bent along a curve on this entity.

The curve passes through `points` (2 to 4096, in the entity's space),
joined by a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline. Copies of the mesh lie end
to end along it, the mesh's x axis along the curve, its y up and its z
across, each stretched along x so a whole number of them spans it; the
curve's frames keep y up. Chunks of at most 256 meters of curve draw
with the material.

material.description: ID of the material its chunks draw with in this document.

mesh.description: ID of the bent mesh in this document.

SceneSpot.description: The cone of a spot light.

direction.description: Direction the cone points in the entity's local space; nonzero.

inner_angle_degrees.description: Half-angle inside which the light is full, in degrees.

outer_angle_degrees.description:
Half-angle beyond which it is dark, in degrees: at least the inner
angle.

SceneSubpixelCulling.description:
Sub-pixel culling settings: whether GPU-presented frames leave visible
instances whose projected bounds cover no pixel center undrawn. They
could produce no fragments, so output is unchanged. On by default.

enabled.description: Whether GPU-presented frames cull sub-pixel instances.

SceneSurface.description:
A material's response to light. Omitted fields keep the
matte defaults: roughness 0.8 and no metalness, emission or ripples.

emission.description: Emitted light as a multiple of the material color.

metalness.description: Metals reflect in their own color and diffuse no light.

roughness.description: 0 is a mirror, 1 spreads highlights and sky reflections widest.

SceneSurroundings.description:
Ground generated past a terrain's edges to the horizon:
a coarser terrain around it from the same layers, its samples four
times as far apart as the terrain's finest, reaching about `reach`
meters past every edge (the terrain's inspection reports how far: its
tiles align with the terrain's sample grids). The terrain's stamps,
heightmaps, bakes and roads fade into its noise over `blend` meters past
its edges (1024 when omitted), so the two meet where it ends. It never
collides, places objects, grows blades or holds water.

SceneTemporalAntialiasing.description:
Temporal antialiasing settings: whether ordinary GPU-presented frames
jitter and resolve against their history, and how the resolve keeps
moving edges and particles from smearing. Its targets cost 16 bytes
per canvas pixel while it runs. Off by default.

enabled.description: Whether ordinary GPU-presented frames resolve temporally.

nearest_motion.description:
Whether each pixel follows the motion of the nearest surface in
the 3x3 pixels around it: the edges of nearer surfaces moving over
farther ones bring their history along instead of leaving a trail,
for nine depth reads a pixel.

particle_response.description:
How strongly particles' coverage of a pixel favors this frame's
color there: the frame's share is at least this times their
coverage, so smoke and spray do not smear as they move. 0 leaves
them as any surface.

rounded_clamp.description:
Whether the history keeps within a box rounded between the range
of the pixel's four edge neighbors and that of all eight: thin and
diagonal features flicker less, for four more reads a pixel.

SceneTerrain.description:
A heightfield terrain on this entity.

Its first corner (least x and z) lies at `origin` in world space,
whatever the entity's transform; heights rise from the origin's y. Its
heights come from `layers`, applied in order to every sample (later
layers win): an imported terrain is a heightmap layer, its known
rivers a rivers layer before its hydrology layer (`terrain_import`
writes both). Its tiles load as records, the cook's
or made by the same jobs. Level-0 tiles span 256 samples `spacing`
meters apart; coarser levels halve the tiles up to one.

collision.description: Whether it collides where collision is installed. Omitted, true.

layers.description: The layers generating its heights, in order; at least one.

surface.description:
Its materials and biomes. Omitted, the engine's default: grass,
bare dirt, rock on steep ground and snow above 650 meters.

surroundings.description: Ground generated around it to the horizon.

tiles.description: Level-0 tiles along x and z. Required.

SceneTerrainAsset.description:
An object placement layers stand on a terrain: a `mesh`
and a `material` of this document, by ID, up to four coarser meshes it
draws at a distance, finest first (otherwise the mesh's automatic levels
of detail), up to two parts drawn with materials of their own, and how
far it sways in the wind: meters at
ten meters up in full wind, 0 (rigid, the default) to 10.

collider.description:
Its objects' collider; without one they never
collide.

shadow.description:
ID of a simpler mesh of this document its objects draw in place of
its levels into shadow maps, opaque and depth only; without one they
cast their own levels.

SceneTerrainCollider.description:
The collider of a placement asset's objects, in its
mesh's space at scale 1: its shape about `center` (the origin by
default), and the collision layers its objects belong to (the first by
default) and collide with (every one by default). Objects within
terrains' collision radius collide; those standing far away never do.

SceneTerrainLayer.description:
One layer of a terrain's stack: procedural noise with erosion, a stamp
(raise, lower, flatten or cut holes), an imported heightmap, rivers
given (drawn, or written by `terrain_import` from vector data) to the
hydrology layer after them, which runs them as given before deriving any
of its own, an erosion
bake of the layers before it, where rivers wear valleys
and slopes creep, a hydrology bake of them, which
carves channels where water gathers, fills lakes and rivers with water
and feeds the `flow`, `wetness` and `lake` masks, a
path: a road leveling the layers before it along its
line, which feeds the `path` mask (the `terrain_route` request finds
routes for them), or relief by cause where the hydrology bake's maps
place it, off its water: rock steps on steep ground and earth hummocks
on wet, gentle ground. Terrains load no tiles until their bakes are done.

SceneTerrainLod.description:
A coarser mesh of a placement asset, by ID, and the largest deviation
from the asset's mesh it shows, in mesh units; errors grow with each.

SceneTerrainMaterial.description:
How one surface material looks: a `material` of this document whose
maps and factors shade it, or a linear `color` and `roughness`; the
meters its textures repeat over (0.01 to 1000); how sharply its height
map wins where it blends with another (0 to 1); whether steep ground
projects it from the side; and the cover growing where it lies.

deform.description: Meters tracks sink it at most: 0, rigid, to 2.

displacement.description:
Meters its maps' heights move the ground itself where that depth
spans a few pixels: 0, none, to 2.

relief.description:
Meters its maps' heights span where the ground's relief shows:
0, flat, to 1.

SceneTerrainMotionDetail.description:
How terrain loads while the camera moves fast: the
finest levels' tiles in its view wait, more of them the faster it
moves, and tiles out of its view wait until it settles. The coarsest
pinned levels, collision's tiles and those under focus entities never
wait, and tiles resident stay.

fastest.description:
Meters per second at which the finest `levels` levels wait, at least
`speed`; between, fewer wait, at least one.

levels.description: Finest levels whose tiles wait at `fastest`.

settle.description:
Seconds after the camera slows below `speed` before tiles out of its
view load.

speed.description: Meters per second above which the camera moves fast.

SceneTerrainPart.description:
A part of a placement asset its objects draw with a `material` of its
own, such as a tree's masked needle cards over its opaque crown: its
meshes by ID, at the asset's mesh and then at each of its coarser
meshes, as far as it reaches; coarser levels draw without it. It takes
the asset's color, sway and impostor, and casts no shadow: the asset's
`shadow`, where it has one, is the whole object's.

bounce.description:
Bounce light, with long sun shadows: probes over each terrain
whose transfer is cooked from its finest pinned level and its
surface's rules, nothing of the sun or sky in it, gather every
frame the light the ground around sends them as the sun, its
shadows and the sky light it now, so slopes the sun lights light
the valleys beside them through the day. They relight in nested
levels around the detail eye, the coarsest over the whole terrain,
so every place takes the same light wherever the eye stands.
Terrain takes its light from the ground around it there, and what
stands on terrain that light and the share of the sky the ground
leaves it. Surroundings, and all ground with bounce light off,
take none.

bounce_columns.description:
Probe columns along each side of every level of probes relit
around the detail eye, an even count: the finest level at the
terrain's own columns, each coarser one twice as far apart and
reaching twice as far, the coarsest holding the whole terrain. A
level shades within half its side, less two and a half columns, of
the eye. Each level's window takes a square of these texels of the
horizon maps (`shadow_resolution` a side); a terrain whose levels
they cannot hold takes no bounce light.

bounce_levels.description:
Levels of probes a terrain relights at most: as many as its
coarsest needs to hold the whole terrain, whose columns grow past
`bounce_columns` where these leave it short.

bounce_spacing.description:
Meters between the finest level's probe columns at most: a terrain
takes the power of two of them along its longer side within this
spacing, at most 512 (larger terrains spread theirs wider). Each
block of two by two columns holds one probe where the ground around
stays open and four where it rises around them, in two layers:
about 100 bytes a probe in the record, 7 to 27 MB a terrain of 512
columns.

cache_bytes.description:
Bytes of tiles kept in memory after the view leaves them,
about 600 KB each, to return at once when it comes back (and
those places games name load into): the least recently used
beyond drop, and 0 keeps none.

collision_radius.description:
Meters around the camera and focus entities within which level-0
tiles load for collision.

gpu_materials.description:
Level-0 tiles' and surroundings' tiles' surface materials from
the GPU: those tiles generate without control values, which a
compute pass gives each as it uploads, the rules' own but where GPU
rounding crosses a threshold; gameplay reads the rules at the
points it asks. Off, the CPU gives them. Either way a terrain's
coarser tiles take theirs from their shading, level 0's averaged,
made in the cook.

loading_work_ms.description:
Milliseconds a frame works on terrain until the camera's view first
loads whole: loading takes large slices of frames.

macro_resolution.description:
Texels along the sides of each terrain's macro color map (the tint
and growth its bakes give its ground over its whole extent),
rounded up to a multiple of four: a byte each with a third more for
their mips on devices sampling compressed textures, four elsewhere.

max_tiles.description:
An optional budget of resident tiles (about 270 KB each, twice that
on the GPU); the least important beyond it drop.

motion_detail.description:
Detail lowered while the camera moves fast: off by
default, as it lowers detail in motion on purpose.

pinned_levels.description:
The coarsest levels kept resident over the whole terrain, so it
always draws whole.

pixel_error.description:
Pixels a level's samples span where its tiles load and shade the
ground, before the next coarser level's take over; smaller loads
finer tiles farther out.

relief_steps.description:
The most steps a ray takes through the ground's relief. Relief
shows by its size on screen, its view rays marching through its
materials' heights: whole while its depth moves the ground two
pixels or more, fading out by half a pixel, with about a step per
pixel it moves.

samples_per_frame.description:
Work decoded between checks of the frame's work time, in samples'
worth (67,000 a file's tile, the rivers' water on a tile about as
much); a frame's whole work where hosts give terrain no clock.

shadow_resolution.description: Texels along a horizon map's sides, 72 bytes each on the GPU.

shadow_softness.description:
Shadow edge height per meter to the slope casting it (the sun's disc
gives 0.0093).

sky_resolution.description: Texels along a sky visibility map's sides, 4 bytes each.

sky_visibility.description:
Ambient light on terrain scaled by how much sky its ground sees,
and taken from the sky it sees: each terrain's sky visibility map,
cooked with its lighting from its finest pinned level, where
valleys and hollows see less sky and take the light of the ground
around them instead, as bounce light gathers it.

subdivision_depth.description:
The deepest level of each terrain's subdivision: two levels halve
its leaves' sides, and each takes twice the memory, a bit for every
leaf it could hold and a quarter more for their counts. 27 holds
leaves a meter across on an 8-kilometer terrain in 20 MB; devices
whose storage bindings hold less keep it shallower, counted.

subdivision_error.description:
Pixels the ground's drawn triangles may stray from its true
surface, seen from the detail eye: each terrain's subdivision
splits its leaves straying more and merges those whose halves
would not, refining a level every other frame. Smaller draws more
triangles.

subdivision_leaves.description:
The most leaves each terrain's subdivision draws, 28 bytes each on
the GPU: past them leaves split no more, counted, and the ground
there stays coarser.

sun_shadows.description:
Long sun shadows through each terrain's horizon map,
with shadows on: the near shadow maps then draw terrain near their
receivers, the kept shadow levels hold its ground as far as they
reach, and the horizon map shadows the rest. Off, terrain casts
into the shadow maps alone. The map holds the
horizons in sixteen directions, cooked with the terrain's lighting
from its finest pinned level, so the sun moves freely.

surroundings.description:
Ground generated around terrains with surroundings
streams and draws; off, every terrain ends at its edges.

upload_bytes.description:
Bytes of tiles becoming resident in a frame, which the GPU takes in
that frame, about 540 KB a tile: tiles beyond wait for the next,
though each frame's first arrives whatever its size.

work_ms.description:
Milliseconds a frame works on terrain after: play takes small
slices.

SceneTerrainSurface.description:
A terrain's surface: up to 255 materials, which biome
layers name by ID, and up to 255 biomes. Later biomes paint over earlier
ones where they fit; the first covers wherever none of the others do.

assets.description: What placement layers stand on the terrain.

bridge.description:
ID of the document material its roads' bridges draw
with; omitted, a weathered stone.

macro_colors.description:
How strongly each cause tints its macro colors (the tint and growth
its bakes and its shape give its ground over its whole extent), and
the side the midday sun stands on. Omitted, the engine's defaults.

placed.description: Objects authors stand on it, each at its own point.

steep.description: The material covering its steep ground over every biome.

SceneTexture.description:
Opaque RGBA8 sRGB pixels in row-major, top-to-bottom order: inline as
base64, or an image file beside the scene that
the host decodes with the platform's own decoder when the scene loads.

Decoding never happens in simulation or rendering. Scenes store one level;
the renderer generates mip levels and samples them trilinearly.

rgba8.description:
Inline pixels: canonical padded RFC 4648 base64; each alpha byte must
equal 255.

uri.description:
An image file (PNG, JPEG or KTX2) as a path relative to the scene,
instead of inline pixels.

SceneTextureMap.description:
A texture map with its sampling and placement. Omitted settings take
glTF's defaults: repeating, trilinear, untransformed.

mipmap_filter.description:
Filtering between mip levels; `none` samples the full-size texture
only.

offset.description:
Texture coordinates are scaled, rotated by `rotation` radians, then
offset.

tex_coord.description:
The texture coordinates the map reads: 0, the mesh's first (the
default), or 1, its second.

latitude.description: The latitude that, with the day, sets the sun's path.

north.description: The yaw of north in the world: degrees from -z toward +x.

speed.description: How many hours pass each second; 0 holds it.

step.description: The minutes of each step the sun moves by.

SceneTopLayer.description:
A layer settling on a material's faces turned up: its
linear color, how far from straight up it reaches (0 covers nothing, 1
every face turned up at all) and its roughness (default 0.85).

SceneTransform.description:
Local transform with Euler XYZ rotation expressed in degrees.

Bounded translations and scales avoid singular or overflowing normal
transforms. Parent composition preserves full matrices, including
shear. Negative scale reflection is not authored by this format.

SceneVertex.description: CPU vertex authoring data; the renderer owns its separate upload layout.

color.description:
Linear RGBA in `[0, 1]` multiplying the material's base
color. Every vertex of a mesh has one or none does.

joints.description:
Up to four joints (indices into the skin of the entities
drawing the mesh) moving this vertex. Every vertex of
a mesh has joints and weights or none does.

uv1.description:
Second texture coordinates, which texture maps may read.
Every vertex of a mesh has them or none does.

weights.description:
The joints' weights, not negative and not all zero; they
are normalized.

SceneVirtualGeometry.description:
Virtual geometry settings: whether meshes built as cluster
hierarchies draw the clusters each view needs, and how coarse those may
be.

enabled.description: Whether meshes with clusters draw as virtual geometry.

pixel_error.description:
The largest simplification error a drawn cluster may show, in pixels
